mechanism: Compete for same absorption transporter (DMT1). Calcium blocks iron uptake by 60%.
recommendation: Take 2 hours apart. Take iron on empty stomach with Vitamin C.

mechanism: Both compete for divalent metal transporter. High zinc reduces iron absorption.
recommendation: Separate by 2 hours. Avoid taking simultaneously.

mechanism: Vitamin C converts Fe3+ to Fe2+ form, increasing absorption by 3x. Beneficial interaction.
recommendation: Take together — Vitamin C enhances iron absorption significantly.

mechanism: Magnesium may slightly reduce iron absorption at high doses.
recommendation: Mild concern. Separate by 1 hour if possible.

mechanism: Vitamin D3 promotes calcium absorption in the intestine. Synergistic.
recommendation: Take together — ideal combination for bone health.

mechanism: High calcium can reduce magnesium absorption and vice versa at high doses.
recommendation: Take with meals. Maintain 2:1 calcium to magnesium ratio.

mechanism: Calcium inhibits zinc transporter ZIP4, reducing zinc bioavailability.
recommendation: Separate by 2 hours. Take zinc on empty stomach.

mechanism: K2 directs calcium (mobilized by D3) to bones instead of arteries. Synergistic and protective.
recommendation: Take together — essential combination, especially at high D3 doses.

mechanism: Magnesium is required to convert Vitamin D to its active form. Deficiency blocks D3 activation.
recommendation: Take together — magnesium activates Vitamin D3.

mechanism: High-dose Vitamin E antagonizes Vitamin K-dependent clotting factors, increasing bleeding risk.
recommendation: Do not take high-dose Vitamin E with Vitamin K2. Consult doctor.

mechanism: Vitamin E protects omega-3 fatty acids from oxidation, preserving potency.
recommendation: Take together — Vitamin E stabilizes fish oil.

mechanism: High zinc blocks copper absorption via metallothionein. Can cause copper deficiency.
recommendation: If taking zinc >40mg, supplement copper. Take 8-12 hours apart.

mechanism: Work together in methylation cycle. B12 deficiency can mask folate status.
recommendation: Take together — synergistic for DNA synthesis and homocysteine control.

mechanism: No direct interaction but iron deficiency impairs Vitamin D receptor function.
recommendation: Take separately to optimize individual absorption.

mechanism: Magnesium required as cofactor for Vitamin D activation enzymes.
recommendation: Take together for optimal D3 activation.

mechanism: High-dose Vitamin C (1000mg+) can destroy B12 in the gut before absorption.
recommendation: Separate by at least 2 hours. Take B12 first, then Vitamin C later.

mechanism: Multivitamins contain calcium/zinc that block iron absorption.
recommendation: Take iron separately 2 hours before or after multivitamin.

mechanism: Multivitamin already contains calcium — risk of exceeding upper limit (2500mg/day).
recommendation: Check total calcium intake. May not need extra calcium supplement.

mechanism: Multivitamins contain Vitamin D — risk of exceeding upper limit (4000 IU/day).
recommendation: Check total Vitamin D. Avoid doubling up without doctor guidance.

mechanism: Omega-3 may enhance Vitamin D absorption as both are fat-soluble.
recommendation: Take together with a meal for best absorption of both.

mechanism: B12 may affect melatonin synthesis through methylation pathways.
recommendation: Take melatonin at bedtime, B12 in the morning.

mechanism: Ashwagandha has some iron content and may support iron levels.
recommendation: Generally safe together.

mechanism: Curcumin chelates iron and can significantly reduce iron absorption.
recommendation: Separate by at least 2 hours. Take iron first.

mechanism: Curcumin may enhance Vitamin D receptor expression.
recommendation: Safe and potentially beneficial together.

mechanism: Both fat-soluble antioxidants that work synergistically.
recommendation: Take together with a fat-containing meal.

mechanism: Compete for same absorption transporter (DMT1).
recommendation: Take 2 hours apart.

mechanism: Vitamin C may enhance zinc absorption slightly.
recommendation: Safe to take together.

mechanism: Compete for absorption at high doses.
recommendation: Maintain 2:1 ratio; take with meals.

mechanism: Zinc may impair folate absorption at high doses.
recommendation: Separate by 1-2 hours if using high-dose zinc.

mechanism: Both B-vitamins, work synergistically in energy metabolism.
recommendation: Safe and beneficial to take together.

mechanism: Prenatal vitamins already contain iron — excessive iron intake risk.
recommendation: Do not add separate iron without doctor supervision.

mechanism: Prenatal vitamins contain calcium — risk of excess.
recommendation: Check total calcium before adding extra supplement.

mechanism: High Vitamin A can antagonize Vitamin D activity at receptor level.
recommendation: Keep Vitamin A at recommended doses. Don't megadose with D3.

mechanism: Both fat-soluble, compete for absorption at very high doses.
recommendation: Take at different meal times if using high doses.

mechanism: Omega-3 and magnesium together support cardiovascular and muscle health.
recommendation: Take together — complementary benefits.
